title: Joining the Saints and Sinners in Pittsburgh in 1963
summary: Afraid since his hip injury to travel, he finally took the bus to Pittsburgh, played nervously on the stand, and by the third night felt he was boss, staying nearly ten years.

blocks.x: Oh, when was this, Herman, that he
Um, thirty what? Thirty -- thirty --
Sixty.
Well did you actually join him in '64? Is that right?
Mary, when did I go with the Saints?

Uh-huh, and he called me. He had Joe -- Joe Thomas, Joe Thomas was on -- was there with him, and had been -- Joe -- well Joe is Joe, you know. He's a hell of a trumpet player. He -- you've got to give it to him. He's -- well, when he has too many tastes, you know, he's another guy, and I think that's what had happened.
And he called me and asked me, are you coming to make it. And -- well I -- at that time I had -- since I'd been home, I hadn't been on the road since I had this broken hip.
I see, and that was in 1950.

Yeah, I -- so I hadn't been back on the road. I did a few jobs around the city here, you know. A few things. And I was afraid -- truthfully, I was afraid to accept anything, and going on the road, I figured I
wouldn't be able to do it.
Tell me, at that point, Herman, did you have trouble getting around?
Well --
How -- were you walking with a cane?
Oh yeah! Man, I was walking as good just like as right now.
You had the built-up shoe?
Yeah.
And a cane?

Uh-huh. So he said come on -- can you get out? I said well, it's too late to get a plane. I said to heck with the plane, man. So I took a bus that morning, here, and I got there around 5:00 o'clock, about 5:00 o'clock. And they didn't hit til 8:00, so they gave me plenty of time.
Where is this, in Columbus?
No, no. Pittsburgh.
Oh, Pittsburgh. I see.

And the station's right down the street from the hotel, you know. It was nothing. So I got in and I went on the stand, and I really did feel nervous, though, because I said I haven't played, really, had -- where -- a place where I had to really cook, in a long time. I said well what the hell. And the money was nice.
(Laughter.)
So I just -- I got to do it. So we got on the stand, and everything went down, first night, second night. The third night I was boss.
(Laughter.)

Yeah! I called the wife, she said how is it? I said fine! Don't worry about it. So I stayed with them then, damn near ten years. And he took me out, and by God, have it here, got a lot of magazines and pictures and stuff here with the band.
